name: Linux kernel source distribution
description: A Unix-like kernel for 386-compatible computers, developed and shared by Linus Torvalds and collaborators, initially under noncommercial redistribution conditions.

date.basis: Date or approximate interval stated by the source for this event.

events.statement: Torvalds announced availability of version 0.02 kernel sources for wider distribution.
events.caveats: Version 0.01 had already circulated to interested people without a broad announcement; the transcription is preserved by a third-party site.

contributions.resource: Developed and publicly announced early kernel sources.

evidence.supports: Post identifies Torvalds and describes his kernel.
Reproduced post announces source availability and notes early supported GNU programs.

date.basis: Date or approximate interval stated by the source for this event.

events.statement: Version 0.12 release notes proposed changing to GNU-compatible copyleft from 1 February 1992, subject to contributor agreement.
events.caveats: This announcement is not evidence of the final legal status of every later contribution; the initial version was not GPL licensed.

evidence.supports: Release notes describe proposed change and consent condition.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated event established in the cited sources for this scoped record; it does not assert global priority.

caveats: A kernel is not a complete distribution; usable systems combined it with additional software. Source availability did not imply zero network or hardware cost.

research.note: Source-backed initial research; independent review is pending. Independent reader checked 0.02 announcement and 0.12 copyright proposal in the transcribed posts; no exact 0.01 public release date inferred.
